metadata.remarks:
Identity Federation defines the capability to accept, validate, and rely upon identity assertions issued by external organizations under defined trust relationships. Federation enables cross-organizational access while preserving local policy control and accountability.

Governance and Responsibility Anchor:
This pattern is the authoritative anchor for roles and responsibilities, SSPPs, standards, procedures, guidelines, and assurance activities related to federated identity. Controls are intentionally scoped to specific federation sub-capabilities.

components.title: Trust Relationships
components.description: Formal establishment and governance of trust relationships with external identity providers.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Establish cryptographically strong trust relationships for identity assertions.
Define and govern federation architecture and trust agreements.

components.title: Assertion Consumption
components.description: Validation and consumption of identity assertions received from trusted external identity providers.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Ensure federated identities are uniquely identified and authenticated.
Protect and validate federated authenticators and assertions.

components.title: External Identity Assurance
components.description: Evaluation of assurance levels and confidence associated with external identity assertions.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Assess and enforce minimum assurance requirements for federated identities.
Incorporate attributes and assurance claims into access decisions.

components.title: Responsibility Boundaries
components.description: Definition and enforcement of responsibility boundaries between the institution and external identity providers.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Define access control responsibilities across organizational boundaries.
Generate audit records for federated access decisions.
